DEVIATIONS / DECISIONS the reviewer should adjudicate:
1. THREE existing tests were rewritten, all because they pinned behaviour the round-3 ruling reverses. (a) PIN T13 (rewritten as the design instructs). Its netting arithmetic (ACTIVE + stored planKey nets against the old plan) remains covered by the untouched PIN T10 ACTIVE cycle-switch test.
2. CARVE-OUT to the subscribe() guard, not stated in the design and worth a ruling: refusing EVERY equal-rank ACTIVE same-cycle pick broke "REG-B58 subscribe() on a planKey-NULL ACTIVE row books the FULL base, not a self-netted 0" (tenantPlan BUSINESS, sub.planKey NULL, picks BUSINESS = equal rank). Refusing that would strand a manual-activation row plan-less forever (it contributes 0 to the MRR snapshot until it gains a planKey, and upgrade() only moves up). So the same-rank refusal fires only when `priorSub.planKey != null`; a different-rank pick is still refused on a planKey-NULL row (that REG-B58 test is untouched and green). The consequence the owner may want to weigh: the equal-rank re-pick was previously the only self-service planVersionId re-pin route, and it is now closed — the re-pin is left to platform-admin updatePlan and the cron.

4. planChangePreview now fetches the published catalog on the UPGRADE, DOWNGRADE, CONTACT_SALES and cycle-switch paths (one call, hoisted, reused by the UPGRADE branch). The SUBSCRIBE/NOOP/KEEP_CURRENT early returns still never touch it — the "SUBSCRIBE / NOOP paths never fetch the published catalog" pin is untouched and green.
5. Removed the now-dead equal-rank SUBSCRIBE branch in planChangePreview: with normalized comparison, rankFrom === rankTo implies samePlan, which is handled above (same cycle) or by the cycle-switch branch.
6. WEB SIDE STILL OWED (not mine): apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts must add "CONTACT_SALES" to its own PlanChangeAction copy and handle it in dispatchPlanChange, and the chooser should mark the current card from the new `preview.change.fromPlanKey`. I tried to refute by looking for a path where `warnings` is non-empty but the return drops it: :562 spreads `...(warnings.length ? { warning: warnings.join(" ") } : {})` on the single DOWNGRADE return — there is no second return in that branch.

subscription-mutation.service.ts:398-399 — planChangePreview normalizes first and throws BadRequestException(`Unknown plan "X"`) before any ranking, so planRank(-1) can never read as "lower than every plan"; downgrade():655-660 adds `if (planRank(targetPlanKey) < 0) throw` immediately after the catalog lookup, so an off-list key that IS published still cannot pass the rank check at :681. Pinned by spec:906-946 with a catalog fixture that pushes a real off-list "PRO" definition, so the def-exists check passes and only the rank check can catch it — the test would fail if the guard were removed. See new hazard #6 for the blast radius of throwing at the top of the method.

newHazards.summary: The new cancellation warning makes the chooser demand a FALSE "users will be deactivated" acknowledgement on a downgrade with no seat problem
newHazards.detail: Introduced by this round's finding 3/12 fix. page.tsx:89 infers the seat consequence from the mere presence of a string: `needsDowngradeAck = changeAction === "DOWNGRADE" && !!preview?.change?.warning`. Round 3 made the API push a SECOND, unrelated string into that same field — subscription-mutation.service.ts:537 pushes CANCELLATION_REVOKED_WARNING whenever priorSub.cancelAtPeriodEnd is true, independently of the seat check at :538-555. Scenario (the round's own headline case): an ACTIVE tenant on SCALE with a cancellation armed and a team of 2 picks STARTER (cap 3). warnings = [cancellation] only; preview.warning is set; needsDowngradeAck becomes true, so page.tsx:301-311 renders the checkbox "I understand these users will be deactivated" and page.tsx:325 blocks the commit until the tenant ticks it — asserting a consequence that will not happen (billing-cron.service.ts:183 only deactivates when activeTeam > seatCap). The tenant is made to consent to a false statement at a money decision point, and the acknowledgement gate loses its meaning for the case it was built for. Fix is small and belongs on the API side of the seam: return the seat consequence as its own signal (e.g. a boolean or a separate field) rather than making the page infer it from `warning` being non-empty.

newHazards.summary: The cycle-switch SUBSCRIBE branch still revokes a pending cancellation and wipes a scheduled downgrade with no warning
newHazards.detail: Findings 3/12 named three branches that silently disarm a pending transition; the ruling covered two. The cycle-switch return at :493-500 carries only "Switching billing cycle takes effect immediately and is not prorated." It commits through subscribe(), whose upsert `update` branch at :290-292 writes cancelAtPeriodEnd: false, downgradeToPlanKey: null, downgradeEffectiveAt: null. So a tenant who cancelled (or scheduled a downgrade) and then flips MONTHLY→ANNUAL on their own plan has the schedule silently called off, with the machinery to say so (CANCELLATION_REVOKED_WARNING, the composed `warnings` list) already sitting two branches below. One line of the same shape as :520 closes it; recording it as a residual is also defensible since the round's ruling scoped only UPGRADE/DOWNGRADE.

newHazards.summary: Web declares a `message` field on PlanChange that the API never sends, and documents it as server-provided
newHazards.detail: The web exec flagged this ambiguity and it resolved against them: the API's CONTACT_SALES return (subscription-mutation.service.ts:477-486) puts the sales copy in `warning`, not `message`. billing.ts:95-97 declares `message?: string` with a docblock asserting it is "Set on CONTACT_SALES", and page.tsx:298-300 renders a block that can never appear. Harmless at runtime (the copy still shows via the amber `warning` line at :294-296) but it is a false contract in the mirror interface — exactly the class of hand-mirrored-shape drift lesson L-072 is about. Either drop `message` from the web interface and its render block, or have the API populate it; do not leave both.

newHazards.summary: `preview` is never cleared and the re-quote has no onError, so a failed quote re-enables the commit button with a stale plan/action and a now-live cycle
newHazards.detail: Residual half of finding 7. Both quote calls (page.tsx:73 and :78) pass only onSuccess — a failed quote leaves `preview` holding the previous plan, action and cycle, and once the request settles `quote.isPending` goes false so the :319-326 disabled guard releases. Round 3 changed the commit body to take `cycle` live (billing.ts:314) while `planKey` and `changeAction` still come from the stale preview, so the committed body can now be a combination the server never quoted: {planKey: <previous selection>, cycle: <new toggle>}. Reachability requires a failed or still-pending-then-failed re-quote, and the button label does keep showing the stale plan name, which is why I score it minor. The ruling's own hint offered the closing move: clear `preview` (and `selected`'s quote) whenever cycle/selected change, or assert preview.planKey === selected before dispatching.

newHazards.summary: The new ACTIVE-only cron filter defers rather than clears a stale schedule: reinstating a suspended tenant re-arms a months-old downgrade
newHazards.detail: Finding 8's fix (billing-cron.service.ts:131) stops the sweep while the tenant is SUSPENDED/CANCELLED/soft-deleted, but nothing clears the markers, and the reinstatement paths do not either: onPaymentSucceeded (billing.service.ts:589-599) and onCheckoutCompleted (:541-549) flip the tenant back to ACTIVE and update the period without touching downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt. The stale downgradeEffectiveAt is by then in the past, so the very next 02:00 tick applies a downgrade the tenant scheduled before they lapsed — rewriting basePriceSnapshot, booking a second PLAN_CHANGED delta, and deactivating every OPERATOR/DRIVER over the target cap (retainedUserIds is []). Pre-existing in shape (before the filter it fired while suspended, which was worse), so this is not a regression introduced by round 3 — but the finding's hint explicitly asked for the disposition decision and the ruling did not make it. Same clear the round already added to activateManualSubscription would close it.

newHazards.summary: Refusing an off-list published key at the top of planChangePreview 400s the whole /billing/quote for every tenant, including the fresh-subscribe path that used to price it correctly
newHazards.detail: The guard sits before the tenant/status branch, so it fires on paths that never rank anything. settings-billing.controller.ts:85-87 calls planChangePreview unconditionally whenever the caller has a tenantId, so the throw takes the entire quote response down. Consequence: publish a catalog definition whose planKey is not in PLAN_KEYS and the chooser 400s for EVERY tenant on that card — including a TRIAL/new tenant whose commit route is subscribe(), which reads the definition from the published catalog and writes basePriceSnapshot: def.monthlyPrice correctly (finding 13 says so itself). One operational mistake now bricks the chooser rather than mis-pricing one downgrade. This is what the ruling asked for ("refused at the seam"), so it is a scope note for the owner, not a defect against the design — but if a softer answer is wanted, returning SUBSCRIBE for an unrankable key in the preview while keeping downgrade():658's hard refusal preserves the money guard and the working path.

review.regateVerdict: Regate is trustworthy for what it covers, and I re-derived its claims rather than taking them: all four gate commands are green (api tsc clean; api jest src/billing src/sales-agents src/platform-admin = 24 suites / 362 tests; web tsc clean; web jest lib/api/billing.test.ts = 10 tests). The pins the executors cite exist and are real oracles, not tautologies — I opened each one: the platform-admin finding-2 pin is an exact toHaveBeenCalledWith plus not.toHaveProperty("cancelAtPeriodEnd") (spec:170-195); the cron finding-8 pin uses toEqual on where.tenant (spec:233); the webhook finding-10 pins assert key ABSENCE on the false-cancel event (spec:169-171); the finding-13 pins push a genuine off-list "PRO" definition into the catalog fixture so only the rank check can catch it (spec:908-945); the finding-3/12 pin asserts both composed warnings in one preview (spec:835-838). The three rewritten tests are all justified — each pinned behaviour the round-3 ruling reverses (PIN T13 rewritten as instructed; the Amendment-2 equal-rank SUBSCRIBE pin is superseded by ruling 5; the ACTIVE-same-plan re-subscribe netting test became a refusal pin, with its arithmetic still covered by the untouched PIN T10 cycle-switch case). Gate blind spots the lead should know: the gate runs only three API path filters and ONE web test file, so nothing exercises apps/web/app/(dashboard)/choose-plan/page.tsx at all — new hazard #1 (the false deactivation acknowledgement) lives entirely in that unexercised file and no gate in this round could have caught it. The E2E spec apps/web/e2e/33-change-plan-routing.spec.ts still passes by inspection (its mocked DOWNGRADE quote carries no `warning`, so needsDowngradeAck stays false), but it too never runs in this lane. The Final gate (full `npx jest` both workspaces + validate-lessons) has not run yet.
review.reasoning: All 13 in-scope findings are genuinely fixed — I tried to refute each by tracing its own failure scenario through the current code and could not break any of them, and every fix carries a pin that would fail if the fix were reverted. The union extension is complete (PlanChangeAction is declared exactly twice, both updated; nothing in packages/ or apps/mobile consumes it), the alias-aware samePlan and the subscribe() same-rank refusal are consistent with each other and leave the cycle-switch branch intact, the platform-admin clears do not fight their existing specs (the cancelAtPeriodEnd omission in updatePlan is deliberate and pinned), and the webhook clears are correctly conditional on Stripe's own arming flag. I recommend one more round for exactly one item: new hazard #1. The round's finding-3/12 fix pushes a second, unrelated string into `change.warning`, and choose-plan/page.tsx:89 uses "warning is non-empty" as its proxy for the seat consequence — so the round's own headline scenario (a tenant with a cancellation armed scheduling a downgrade while comfortably under the seat cap) now forces them to tick "I understand these users will be deactivated" when nobody will be deactivated, and blocks the commit until they do. That is a false statement demanded as consent on the money path, introduced by this round, in a file no gate in this lane exercises. The fix is small and belongs on the API side of the seam — return the seat consequence as its own field rather than making the page infer it from `warning` — plus the page reading that field at :89. Everything else I found is minor and recordable as residuals rather than blocking: the cycle-switch branch's missing cancellation notice (same class, out of the ruling's two-branch scope), the dead `message` field on the web mirror, the stale-preview-after-a-failed-quote window that finding 7's ruling left half-open, the schedule stranded on a lapsed-then-reinstated tenant (finding 8's undecided second half), and the blast radius of throwing on an off-list published key at the top of planChangePreview. If the lead prefers to land now, hazard #1 is the only one I would not ship without a note to the owner, and the Final gate (full jest in both workspaces + validate-lessons) still has to run either way.
